lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: Luke says many have set out an account, that eyewitnesses and ministers of the word handed it down, and that he writes in order so Theophilus may know the certainty of what he was taught.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Luke wrote and who he says handed the story down?
ev: Name the reason Luke gives for writing and the sources he mentions.

nodes.t: Gabriel Promises a Son to Zacharias
nodes.d: While Zacharias serves in the temple at the hour of incense, the angel Gabriel says Elisabeth will bear a son, John; Zacharias doubts, is struck dumb, and Elisabeth conceives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Gabriel told Zacharias and what happened to him because he doubted?
ev: Retell the angel's message, Zacharias's question and its result.

nodes.d: In the sixth month Gabriel tells the virgin Mary, betrothed to Joseph of David's house, that she will bear Jesus, who will receive David's throne and be called Son of the Highest; Mary submits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel told Mary about her son and how she responded?
ev: Say what the angel promised about Jesus and how Mary answered.

nodes.d: Mary hurries to Elisabeth's house; the child leaps in Elisabeth's womb, Elisabeth blesses Mary, and Mary praises God for mercy, for scattering the proud and lifting the lowly, and for remembering Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Mary's visit to Elisabeth and name things Mary praises God for?
ev: Retell the meeting and name two things Mary praises God for in her song.

nodes.d: Elisabeth bears a son, the family insists on the name John, Zacharias's tongue is loosed, and he blesses God for the horn of salvation, the oath to Abraham, and his son who will go before the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Zacharias spoke again and what he said about John and God's promise?
ev: Describe how Zacharias regained speech and what he said about God's covenant and about John.

nodes.t: The Birth of Jesus and the Shepherds
nodes.d: A decree brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger; angels announce a Saviour, Christ the Lord, to shepherds, who go and tell what they saw.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the birth of Jesus and the shepherds' part in it?
ev: Retell the birth, the angel's announcement and what the shepherds did.

nodes.t: Simeon and Anna in the Temple
nodes.d: Jesus is named and presented at the temple; Simeon, to whom the Spirit promised he would see the Lord's Christ, blesses God for salvation for all peoples, and Anna the prophetess speaks of him to those awaiting redemption.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Simeon and Anna said when they saw the child Jesus?
ev: Say what Simeon was waiting for and what he and Anna said.

nodes.t: The Boy Jesus in the Temple
nodes.d: At twelve, Jesus stays in Jerusalem after the Passover and is found after three days among the teachers; he tells his parents he must be about his Father's business and then returns home subject to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Jesus at twelve in the temple?
ev: Retell where Jesus was found and what he said, and how he lived afterwards.

nodes.t: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
nodes.d: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius the word comes to John, who preaches a baptism of repentance, calls for fruits worthy of repentance, answers the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers, points to one mightier, and is imprisoned by Herod.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain John's message of repentance and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: List what John told the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers to do and what he said about the coming one.

nodes.d: When the people were baptized, Jesus is baptized and prays; heaven opens, the Holy Ghost descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven calls him beloved Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened when Jesus was baptized?
ev: Say what happened at Jesus' baptism and what the voice said.

nodes.d: Luke lists Jesus' descent, as was supposed from Joseph, back through David, Abraham, Noe and Seth to Adam, who was the son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the genealogy in Luke 3 ends with and name some people on the list?
ev: Say where the list begins, which famous names it passes, and where it ends.

nodes.d: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is tempted forty days by the devil and answers each of three temptations with 'It is written' and a word of Scripture; the devil departs for a season.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the three temptations and how Jesus answered them?
ev: Name the three temptations and how Jesus answered each.

nodes.d: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?
ev: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.

nodes.d: Jesus teaches with authority in the Capernaum synagogue, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's wife's mother and many at sunset, and tells the crowds he must preach the kingdom to other cities.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus did in Capernaum and say why he went on to other cities?
ev: Name what Jesus did in Capernaum and why he moved on.

nodes.t: The Great Catch and the First Disciples
nodes.d: After teaching from Simon's boat, Jesus tells him to let down the nets; a huge catch breaks them, Peter confesses he is a sinful man, and Simon, James and John leave all to follow Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the great catch of fish and the call of Simon, James and John?
ev: Retell the catch and what Jesus said to Simon and what the fishermen did.

nodes.d: A man full of leprosy asks Jesus, if he is willing, to make him clean; Jesus touches him and he is cleansed, and is told to show himself to the priest as Moses commanded.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the leper?
ev: Say what the leper asked and what Jesus did and told him.

nodes.t: The Paralytic Let Down Through the Roof
nodes.d: Friends lower a paralysed man through the tiles; Jesus forgives his sins, answers the scribes' charge of blasphemy by showing the Son of man has power to forgive sins, and tells the man to rise and walk.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Jesus both forgave the man's sins and healed him?
ev: Explain why Jesus healed him after forgiving his sins.

nodes.t: Levi's Feast and the Question of Fasting
nodes.d: Jesus calls the tax collector Levi, who gives a feast; asked why he eats with sinners, Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance, and he speaks of the bridegroom and of new wine and old wineskins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain whom Jesus came to call and what his sayings about the bridegroom and new wine mean in the passage?
ev: Say who Jesus came to call, and what he said about the bridegroom and new wine.

nodes.d: The disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, and Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath; on another sabbath he heals a withered hand, asking whether it is lawful to do good or evil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe both sabbath conflicts and what Jesus claimed?
ev: Describe the two sabbath conflicts and what Jesus said in each.

nodes.d: After a night in prayer on a mountain, Jesus calls his disciples and names twelve apostles, including Simon Peter, Matthew and Judas Iscariot the traitor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name several of the twelve and say how Jesus prepared for choosing them?
ev: Say what Jesus did before choosing the twelve and name some of them.

nodes.t: Blessings and Woes on the Plain
nodes.d: Jesus blesses the poor, hungry, weeping and hated for his sake, and pronounces woe on the rich, full, laughing and well-spoken-of.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the blessings and woes Jesus gives in Luke 6?
ev: Compare who Jesus calls blessed with who he calls woe.

nodes.d: Jesus tells his hearers to love enemies, bless those who curse them, do to others as they would have done to them, lend without hope of return, be merciful as the Father is, and not judge or condemn but forgive and give.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus commands about enemies and judging others?
ev: Say what Jesus commands about enemies, mercy and judging.

nodes.t: The Blind Guide, the Tree, and Two Builders
nodes.d: Jesus uses sayings about blind guides, a log and a speck, trees known by fruit, and a good treasure of the heart, and ends with the builder on rock who hears and does his words versus the builder with no foundation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two builders and why hearing without doing is not enough?
ev: Explain what Jesus says separates the wise builder from the foolish one.

nodes.d: A centurion sends elders and friends to ask Jesus to heal his servant, saying a word is enough since he himself is under authority; Jesus marvels at such faith and the servant is found well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the centurion's request and Jesus' response?
ev: Say what the centurion believed about Jesus' word and how Jesus responded.

nodes.t: Jesus Raises the Widow's Son at Nain
nodes.d: Seeing a widow carrying out her only son, Jesus has compassion, touches the bier and tells the young man to arise; he sits up and speaks, and the people say God has visited his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the raising of the widow's son at Nain?
ev: Retell what Jesus did at Nain and what the crowd said.

nodes.d: John in prison sends two disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the healings and the gospel preached to the poor, then calls John more than a prophet, the messenger sent before him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John's question and what he said about John?
ev: Say how Jesus answered John's disciples and what he said about John.

nodes.t: The Woman Who Anointed Jesus' Feet
nodes.d: At Simon the Pharisee's house a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with tears and anoints them; Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven and says her many sins are forgiven for she loved much.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the story of the two debtors and how Jesus applied it?
ev: Explain the parable of two debtors and how it applies to Simon and the woman.

nodes.d: Jesus tours with the twelve and women who minister to him, and tells of a sower whose seed falls on four soils; he explains the seed is the word of God and the soils are ways of hearing, and tells them to take heed how they hear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the four soils in the parable of the sower and say what Jesus says each means?
ev: Name the four soils and what each stands for according to Jesus.

nodes.d: When his mother and brothers cannot reach him for the crowd, Jesus says those who hear the word of God and do it are his mother and brothers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jesus calls his family and why?
ev: Say whom Jesus calls his mother and brothers.

nodes.d: Crossing the lake, Jesus sleeps as a storm fills the boat; the disciples wake him, he rebukes wind and waves, and they marvel and wonder who he is.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the calming of the storm?
ev: Retell the storm and what the disciples asked afterwards.

nodes.d: In the country of the Gadarenes Jesus frees a man possessed by a legion of demons; they enter swine that rush into the lake, and the healed man is told to return home and tell what God has done.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the man called Legion?
ev: Retell what happened to the man and the swine and what Jesus told the man to do.

nodes.t: Jairus' Daughter and the Woman with the Issue
nodes.d: Jairus asks Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman with twelve years of bleeding touches his garment and is healed, and then Jesus raises the girl from death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the woman and the raising of Jairus' daughter?
ev: Say what happened to the woman and to Jairus' daughter and what Jesus told Jairus.

nodes.t: The Twelve Are Sent Out; Herod Is Perplexed
nodes.d: Jesus gives the twelve power and sends them to preach and heal, taking nothing for the journey; Herod hears of him and is perplexed, saying he beheaded John.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve and why Herod was perplexed?
ev: Say what the twelve were told to bring and do, and what Herod said.

nodes.d: When the crowd follows Jesus to a desert place, he tells the twelve to give them food; five loaves and two fishes are blessed and broken, all are filled, and twelve baskets of fragments remain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand?
ev: Retell what Jesus did with the loaves and fishes and how much was left.

nodes.t: Peter Confesses the Christ; Take Up the Cross
nodes.d: Jesus asks who people say he is; Peter answers 'The Christ of God', and Jesus says the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise, and that his followers must deny themselves and take up their cross daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Peter's confession and what Jesus said discipleship costs?
ev: Say what Peter confessed, what Jesus foretold, and what he asked of followers.

nodes.d: About eight days later Jesus takes Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray; his appearance changes, Moses and Elias speak with him of his decease at Jerusalem, and a voice from the cloud says 'hear him'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration and what the voice from the cloud said?
ev: Say who appeared with Jesus, what they talked about, and what the voice said.

nodes.t: The Boy with the Spirit; Who Is Greatest
nodes.d: Coming down the mountain, Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not help, again tells them he will be delivered into men's hands, and answers their argument about greatness by setting a child beside him and telling John not to forbid one who casts out demons in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught the disciples about greatness using the child?
ev: Say how Jesus answered the dispute about who is greatest.

nodes.d: As the time comes for him to be received up, Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem; a Samaritan village refuses him and he rebukes James and John for wanting fire, then answers three would-be followers about the cost of following.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Jesus turning toward Jerusalem and what he said to those who wanted to follow?
ev: Say what happened in Samaria and what Jesus told the three would-be followers.

nodes.d: Jesus sends seventy others two by two ahead of him with instructions like those given the twelve, pronounces woe on unrepentant towns, and when they return rejoicing tells them rather to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the seventy and what he said to rejoice about?
ev: Say what the seventy were told to do and what Jesus said they should rejoice in.

nodes.d: Asked by a lawyer what he must do to inherit eternal life, Jesus draws out love of God and neighbour; to the question 'who is my neighbour' he tells of a Samaritan who helps a man left by robbers after a priest and a Levite pass by.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the good Samaritan and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do?
ev: Retell the parable and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do.

nodes.d: Martha is distracted by serving and asks Jesus to tell Mary to help; Jesus says Martha is troubled about many things but one thing is needful and Mary has chosen it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said to Martha about Mary?
ev: Say what Jesus told Martha about Mary's choice.

nodes.d: Asked by a disciple how to pray, Jesus gives a prayer to the Father about his name, kingdom, bread, forgiveness and temptation, and teaches persistence with the friend at midnight and the Father who gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about how to pray?
ev: Say what the prayer asks for and what Jesus says about asking and seeking.

nodes.t: Casting Out Demons: Beelzebub and the Sign of Jonas
nodes.d: After Jesus casts out a mute spirit, some say he does it by Beelzebub; he answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he casts out by the finger of God, refuses a sign except the sign of Jonas, and speaks of light and the eye.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the charge about Beelzebub and Jesus' answer?
ev: Say the charge made against Jesus and how he answered it.

nodes.t: Woes on the Pharisees and Lawyers
nodes.d: At a Pharisee's table Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside while inside is full of wickedness and tithing herbs while neglecting judgment and the love of God, and the lawyers for burdening men and building the prophets' tombs; the scribes begin to lie in wait for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the faults Jesus names in the Pharisees and lawyers?
ev: List some things Jesus faults the Pharisees and lawyers for.

nodes.t: Fear God, Not Men; Confess Christ
nodes.d: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees, says nothing hidden will stay hidden, tells his friends to fear the One who has power after death, assures them God knows every sparrow and hair, and promises the Holy Ghost will teach them what to say.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Jesus says to fear and what he says about sparrows?
ev: Say who Jesus tells his friends to fear and why they need not be afraid.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Rich Fool
nodes.d: Asked to settle an inheritance, Jesus warns against covetousness and tells of a rich man who plans bigger barns and is told 'thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the rich fool and what it warns against?
ev: Say what the rich man planned and what God said to him.

nodes.t: Do Not Be Anxious; Treasure in Heaven
nodes.d: Jesus tells the disciples not to be anxious for food or clothing, pointing to ravens and lilies, to seek the kingdom, and to give alms, for where treasure is, the heart will be also.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about worry using ravens and lilies?
ev: Say what Jesus points to about God's care and what he says to seek first.

nodes.d: Jesus teaches being ready like servants awaiting their master's return, with the thief and the faithful steward as examples, and says to whom much is given much will be required.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about being ready for the Son of man?
ev: Say what Jesus says about readiness and about the faithful and unfaithful servant.

nodes.t: Fire, Division and Reading the Times
nodes.d: Jesus says he came to send fire and has a baptism to undergo, that his coming will bring division even in households, rebukes the crowd for reading the sky but not the time, and urges settling with an adversary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus says about division and what the crowd failed to discern?
ev: Say what Jesus says about division and about discerning the time.

nodes.t: Repent or Perish; The Barren Fig Tree
nodes.d: Told about Galileans killed by Pilate and eighteen killed by a tower, Jesus says those victims were not worse sinners and everyone must repent or perish, then tells of a fig tree given one more year to bear fruit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the Galileans and the tower and the fig tree?
ev: Say what Jesus says about those who died and what the fig-tree parable shows.

nodes.d: Jesus heals a woman bound by a spirit for eighteen years in a synagogue on the sabbath; he answers the ruler's indignation by pointing to loosing an ox on the sabbath and calls her a daughter of Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the bent woman and Jesus' reply?
ev: Retell the healing and Jesus' answer to the ruler of the synagogue.

nodes.d: Jesus compares the kingdom of God to a grain of mustard seed that grows into a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the mustard seed and leaven parables?
ev: Describe the two kingdom pictures Jesus gives.

nodes.t: The Narrow Door and Lament over Jerusalem
nodes.d: Journeying toward Jerusalem, Jesus tells those asking if few are saved to strive to enter the narrow gate before the master shuts the door, says people will come from every direction to the kingdom, calls Herod a fox, and laments over Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the narrow door and his lament over Jerusalem?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the narrow gate and what he laments over Jerusalem.

nodes.t: Healing on the Sabbath and Humility at the Table
nodes.d: At a chief Pharisee's house Jesus heals a man with dropsy, and tells guests not to seek the highest seats and hosts to invite the poor, since the humble will be exalted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about humility at the Pharisee's meal?
ev: Say what Jesus did for the man with dropsy and what he taught about seats and invitations.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Great Supper
nodes.d: A man gives a great supper and invited guests make excuses about land, oxen and marriage, so the master sends servants to bring in the poor, maimed, lame and blind, and then those in the highways, and none of the first invited will taste it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the great supper and who was brought in?
ev: Say what excuses were given and who was invited instead.

nodes.d: To the great crowds Jesus says a disciple must put him before family and his own life, bear his cross, count the cost like a tower-builder or king going to war, and forsake all; salt that loses its savour is thrown out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the tower builder and king illustrations about counting the cost?
ev: List what Jesus says a disciple must be ready to give up and the two cost-counting pictures.

nodes.t: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
nodes.d: When Pharisees murmur that Jesus receives sinners, he tells of a shepherd seeking one lost sheep and a woman seeking one lost coin, and says there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the two parables of the lost sheep and coin and what they show about heaven?
ev: Say why Jesus told these parables and what the joy in heaven is over.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
nodes.d: A younger son takes his inheritance, wastes it, feeds swine, and returns repenting; the father runs to welcome him with robe, ring and feast, while the elder brother angrily refuses to join and the father pleads with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the prodigal son and name what the father does for each son?
ev: Retell the parable and say what the father says to each son.

nodes.t: The Unjust Steward and Serving Two Masters
nodes.d: Jesus tells his disciples of a steward who reduces his master's debtors' bills and is commended for shrewdness, then teaches faithfulness in little and says no one can serve God and mammon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about money and faithfulness after the steward parable?
ev: Say what Jesus draws from the steward and what he says about two masters.

nodes.t: The Pharisees' Pride and the Law Stands
nodes.d: The covetous Pharisees deride Jesus, who says God knows their hearts and what men esteem is abomination to him, that the law and prophets were until John, and that not a tittle of the law will fail.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus tells the Pharisees about their hearts and the law?
ev: Say how Jesus answers the Pharisees who mocked him.

nodes.d: Jesus tells of a rich man and a beggar named Lazarus who both die; Lazarus is carried to Abraham's bosom and the rich man is in torment, where Abraham says a great gulf is fixed and that his brothers have Moses and the prophets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich man and Lazarus and what Abraham said about Moses and the prophets?
ev: Retell the parable and what Abraham says about Moses and the prophets.

nodes.d: Jesus warns against causing little ones to stumble, tells his disciples to rebuke and forgive a repenting brother even seven times a day, and answers a request for more faith with the mustard seed and the servant who does his duty.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about offences, forgiveness and faith?
ev: Say what Jesus teaches about forgiving and about faith as a mustard seed.

nodes.d: Ten lepers cry for mercy and Jesus sends them to the priests; as they go they are cleansed, and only one, a Samaritan, returns to give thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the ten lepers and who came back to give thanks?
ev: Retell what happened to the ten and what Jesus said about the one who returned.

nodes.t: The Kingdom's Coming and the Days of the Son of Man
nodes.d: Asked when the kingdom comes, Jesus says it does not come with observation and is in the midst of them, then tells the disciples the Son of man will be revealed suddenly like lightning, as in the days of Noe and Lot, after he first suffers and is rejected.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noe and Lot?
ev: Say how Jesus describes the coming of the Son of man and what examples he uses.

nodes.d: Jesus tells a parable that men ought always to pray and not faint: a widow keeps asking an unjust judge until he avenges her, and God will avenge his elect speedily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the widow and the judge and what it teaches about prayer?
ev: Say what the parable teaches about prayer.

nodes.d: Two men pray in the temple: a Pharisee thanking God he is not like others, and a tax collector beating his breast and asking mercy; Jesus says the publican went home justified and that the self-exalted will be humbled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified and why?
ev: Contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified.

nodes.d: When people bring infants to Jesus and the disciples rebuke them, Jesus calls the children to him and says the kingdom belongs to such and must be received as a little child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said when children were brought to him?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the children and receiving the kingdom.

nodes.d: A ruler asks what to do to inherit eternal life, says he has kept the commandments, and is told to sell all and follow; he goes away sorrowful, and Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom but possible with God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich ruler and Jesus' words about what is impossible and possible?
ev: Retell what the ruler asked, what Jesus told him and what Jesus said is possible with God.

nodes.d: Jesus tells the twelve they go up to Jerusalem where things written by the prophets will be accomplished: he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, killed, and rise the third day, but they understand none of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve about Jerusalem and what they understood?
ev: List what Jesus says will happen and how the disciples responded.

nodes.d: A blind beggar near Jericho calls Jesus 'thou son of David', persists when rebuked, asks to receive his sight, and is healed; he follows Jesus glorifying God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the blind man near Jericho?
ev: Say what the blind man called Jesus and what happened.

nodes.d: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus; Jesus invites himself to his house, Zacchaeus promises half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution, and Jesus says the Son of man came to seek and save the lost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Zacchaeus and what Jesus said about seeking the lost?
ev: Say what Zacchaeus did and what Jesus said he came to do.

nodes.d: Because he is near Jerusalem and people expect the kingdom to appear, Jesus tells of a nobleman who gives ten servants a pound each before going away to receive a kingdom; on his return he rewards the faithful, rebukes the servant who hid his pound, and deals with the citizens who refused him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the pounds?
ev: Say what each servant did with the pound and what the nobleman did on his return.

nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt, rides it toward Jerusalem as the disciples spread clothes and praise God, saying 'Blessed be the King that cometh', and weeps over the city that does not know the things of its peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry to Jerusalem and why he wept?
ev: Retell the entry and say why Jesus wept over Jerusalem.

nodes.d: Jesus enters the temple and drives out those selling, saying his house is a house of prayer but they made it a den of thieves, and teaches there daily while the chief priests seek to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus did in the temple and what he said about it?
ev: Say what Jesus did in the temple and what he said.

nodes.d: In the temple the chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or men, they will not answer, and so he will not tell them either.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about John's baptism and why the leaders were trapped?
ev: Say what Jesus asked and why the leaders would not answer.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
nodes.d: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants are beaten and sent away and whose beloved son is killed by the tenants; he says the owner will destroy them and give the vineyard to others, and cites the rejected stone that becomes the head of the corner.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the tenants and say what Jesus said about the rejected stone?
ev: Say what the tenants did to the servants and the son and what Jesus said about the stone.

nodes.d: Spies sent by the scribes and chief priests ask whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin, asks whose image it bears, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the tribute question and Jesus' answer?
ev: Say how Jesus answered and why they could not trap him.

nodes.t: The Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection
nodes.d: The Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, ask whose wife a woman married to seven brothers would be; Jesus says those counted worthy of that world neither marry nor die, and the dead are raised, as Moses called the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' answer to the Sadducees about the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the resurrection and how he used Moses.

nodes.t: David's Lord and Beware the Scribes
nodes.d: Jesus asks how Christ can be David's son when David calls him Lord in the Psalms, and warns the disciples about scribes who love long robes and best seats and devour widows' houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about David calling Christ Lord and his warning about scribes?
ev: Say the question Jesus asks about David and what he warns about the scribes.

nodes.d: Jesus sees rich men giving gifts and a poor widow giving two mites, and says she gave more than all of them because she gave all she had.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the widow's offering and why Jesus praised it?
ev: Say why Jesus said the widow gave more than the rich.

nodes.t: The Temple Foretold to Fall; Signs and Persecution
nodes.d: As some admire the temple's stones, Jesus says none will be left on another; asked when, he warns about deceivers, wars and signs, and tells the disciples they will be brought before rulers, given words and wisdom, and not lose a hair of their heads.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize what Jesus foretold about the temple and about persecution?
ev: Say what Jesus says will happen to the temple and what he tells disciples about persecution.

nodes.t: Jerusalem Surrounded and the Son of Man Coming
nodes.d: Jesus says when Jerusalem is surrounded by armies the disciples should flee, that days of vengeance will come, that they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power, and tells them to watch and pray; he gives the fig tree parable and says his words will not pass away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about Jerusalem, his coming, and watching and praying?
ev: Say what the disciples are told to do and what they are told to watch for.

nodes.d: As Passover approaches, the chief priests and scribes seek to kill Jesus; Satan enters Judas Iscariot, who agrees with them to betray Jesus for money.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Judas came to offer to betray Jesus?
ev: Say who plotted, what Judas agreed to, and what the text says entered Judas.

nodes.d: Jesus prepares and eats the Passover with the twelve, saying he desired to eat it before he suffers, and gives bread as his body and the cup as 'the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you'; he says one at the table will betray him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did and said at the Passover meal in Luke 22?
ev: Say what Jesus said over the bread and the cup and what he said about the betrayer.

nodes.t: Who Is Greatest: One Who Serves
nodes.d: The disciples dispute who is greatest; Jesus contrasts Gentile kings with himself as one who serves, promises them a kingdom, tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him but he prayed for his faith, and foretells Peter's three denials.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' teaching on greatness and his words to Peter?
ev: Say what Jesus said about greatness and what he told Peter.

nodes.t: Prayer on the Mount of Olives
nodes.d: On the Mount of Olives Jesus prays 'Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup... not my will, but thine be done'; an angel strengthens him, he prays in agony, and he finds the disciples asleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives?
ev: Say what Jesus prayed and what he told the disciples.

nodes.d: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off the high priest's servant's ear, Jesus heals it, and says to the leaders that this is their hour and the power of darkness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus and what he did for the wounded servant?
ev: Say how Judas betrayed Jesus and what Jesus did for the servant.

nodes.d: Jesus is taken to the high priest's house; Peter follows afar and three times denies knowing him, the cock crows, the Lord looks at him, and Peter weeps bitterly; Jesus is mocked and struck.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Peter's denials and what he did after the cock crowed?
ev: Retell Peter's three denials and what happened after the third.

nodes.d: At day the elders, chief priests and scribes bring Jesus before their council and ask if he is the Christ and the Son of God; he says the Son of man will sit at God's right hand and answers 'Ye say that I am'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the council asked Jesus and how he answered?
ev: Say what the council asked and how Jesus answered.

nodes.d: The crowd accuses Jesus before Pilate, who three times finds no fault; he is sent to Herod, who mocks him, and Pilate at last releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the trial before Pilate and Herod and who was released?
ev: Say what Pilate repeatedly said and who was released.

nodes.d: Jesus is led to Calvary with Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross, prays 'Father, forgive them', is mocked, and tells the repentant criminal beside him that today he will be with him in paradise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said on the cross to the Father and to the criminal?
ev: Say what Jesus said for those crucifying him and to the repentant criminal.

nodes.d: Darkness falls, the temple veil is torn, Jesus cries 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit' and dies; the centurion glorifies God, and Joseph of Arimathaea lays the body in a new rock tomb as the women watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the death of Jesus and his burial?
ev: Say what signs and words marked Jesus' death and who buried him.

nodes.d: On the first day of the week the women find the stone rolled away and are told by two men in shining garments that Jesus is risen; the apostles think it idle talk, but Peter runs to the tomb and sees the linen clothes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the women found at the tomb and what they were told?
ev: Say what the women found and were told and how the apostles reacted.

nodes.d: Two disciples walk to Emmaus when Jesus joins them unrecognised; he explains from Moses and all the prophets the things concerning himself, and their eyes are opened when he breaks bread; they return to Jerusalem to tell the eleven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the Emmaus road and how Jesus opened the Scriptures?
ev: Say how the two disciples recognised Jesus and what he explained to them.

nodes.d: Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his hands and feet and eats fish, opens their minds to the Scriptures, tells them repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and is carried up to heaven as he blesses them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said to the disciples before ascending and how he left them?
ev: Say what Jesus showed them, what he told them to preach, and how he left.

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: Cain murders his brother Abel after God accepts Abel's offering and not his own.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Cain did and how God responded?
ev: Retell the story, including God's question to Cain (4:9)

nodes.d: God sees the wickedness of man, finds favour with Noah, and saves him and his household in the ark through the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Noah and the ark?
ev: Retell why God sent the flood and how Noah and his family were saved
Say how Noah left the ark and what he did (8:20)

nodes.d: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac; God provides a ram in his place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God provided on the mountain?
ev: Retell the story, including 22:8 and 22:13-14

nodes.d: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?
ev: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham

nodes.d: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name from it, declares the ground holy, identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and says he has seen Israel's affliction and will send Moses to Pharaoh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the burning bush and what God said to Moses there?
ev: Describe what Moses saw and what God told him to do with his shoes (3:2-5)
Say what God said he had seen and heard (3:7-9)
Say what God sent Moses to do (3:10)

nodes.t: The firstborn and the feast of unleavened bread
nodes.d: God says all the firstborn of man and beast are his; the firstborn of men are to be redeemed and an ass's firstling redeemed with a lamb. Israel is to remember the day of the exodus, keep the feast of unleavened bread and tell their sons what the LORD did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the firstborn belonged to the LORD and what children were to be told?
ev: Say what God claimed as his in 13:2
Say what Israelites were to tell their sons (13:8, 13:14-15)

nodes.d: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?
ev: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)

nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.d: Leviticus 12 sets the days of uncleanness after the birth of a son or daughter, circumcision on the eighth day, and the lamb and bird (or two birds if poor) offered for her cleansing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what a woman did at the end of the days of purifying?
ev: State when a boy is to be circumcised according to 12:3.
Say what offerings she brings and what changes if she cannot afford a lamb.

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Hear, O Israel: love the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 6 gives the great command to love the LORD with all heart, soul and might because he is one LORD, to teach the words to children throughout the day, to remember him when blessed in the land, and to answer a child's question with the story of the exodus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to love the LORD with all one's heart, soul and might?
ev: Say the command of 6:4-5 in your own words.
List the ways 6:6-9 says to keep the words before oneself and the children.

nodes.t: Remember the wilderness; do not forget
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 8 calls Israel to remember how the LORD humbled and fed them with manna for forty years so they would learn that man lives by every word from the LORD's mouth, and warns against pride and forgetting him in the good land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to remember the wilderness before they entered the land?
ev: Say what the manna was meant to teach (8:3).
Say what danger Moses warns about in 8:11-18.

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow at Zarephath with only a handful of meal and a little oil; at his word she feeds him first, and the barrel and cruse do not run out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the widow's meal and oil, and why?
ev: Retell what the widow had and what happened to it
Say whose word the meal and oil followed (17:14, 16)

nodes.d: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?
ev: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear

nodes.d: Naaman, the Syrian commander, hears from an Israelite servant girl of the prophet in Samaria, goes to Elisha and is told to wash seven times in Jordan; he is angry but obeys and is healed, and confesses there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Gehazi takes a reward by deceit and Naaman's leprosy comes on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Naaman, the servant girl and Gehazi?
ev: Retell why Naaman was angry and what changed his mind
Say what happened to Gehazi and why (5:20-27)

nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 31: into thine hand I commit my spirit
nodes.d: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD as rock and fortress, commits his spirit into his hand, describes distress, reproach and fear on every side, says his times are in the LORD’s hand, and blesses him for his goodness laid up for those who fear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that “my times are in thy hand” in Psalm 31:15?
ev: Read 31:5, 31:15 and 31:19 and state what each says about trusting the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 91: he that dwells in the secret place of the most High
nodes.d: The one who dwells in the secret place of the most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty, who is his refuge and fortress; he will not fear the terror by night or the arrow by day, God gives his angels charge over him, and the LORD speaks of delivering him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 91:1-2 says about the person who trusts in the LORD?
ev: Read 91:1-2 and 91:14-16 and list what the one who trusts receives.

nodes.t: Psalm 110: sit at my right hand; a priest after Melchizedek
nodes.d: The LORD says to the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool; he is a king sent to rule from Zion and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 110:1 and 110:4 and say what the LORD says to the speaker’s Lord?
ev: Read 110:1-4 and say who speaks and to whom, and what is sworn.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Foreigners and eunuchs welcomed; blind watchmen
nodes.d: The LORD says foreigners and eunuchs who hold to his covenant and keep sabbaths will be joyful in his house of prayer for all peoples, while blind watchmen and greedy shepherds are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the LORD welcomes in Isaiah 56:3-8 and what his house is called?
ev: Say who is welcomed in Isaiah 56:3-7
Quote what the house is called (56:7)
Describe the charge against the watchmen (56:10-12)

nodes.t: The Spirit is upon me: good tidings to the meek
nodes.d: A speaker anointed by the Spirit proclaims good tidings to the poor and release for captives, the year of the LORD's favour and a day of vengeance, and the mourners are given beauty for ashes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the one anointed by the Spirit proclaims in Isaiah 61:1-3?
ev: List what the anointed one announces in Isaiah 61:1-3
Say what the people are called in 61:6
Describe the everlasting covenant in 61:8-9

nodes.d: At the gate of the LORD's house Jeremiah says not to trust "the temple of the LORD"; the LORD cites Shiloh, forbids Jeremiah to pray for the people, and condemns worship of the queen of heaven and child burning in Tophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah told the people not to trust in the temple of the LORD in Jeremiah 7:1-15?
ev: Explain what the people trusted and what the LORD required (7:3-7)
Say how the LORD compares the temple to Shiloh (7:12-14)
Describe the sins at Tophet (7:30-34)

nodes.d: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?
ev: Notice the pattern of 'Wherein?' questions (1:2, 1:6, 2:17, 3:7-8)
Say how the book ends (4:5-6)

nodes.d: The LORD announces a messenger to prepare the way before him and the LORD coming suddenly to his temple, like a refiner's fire who purifies the sons of Levi; he will be a swift witness against sinners, for he does not change.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who is coming in Malachi 3:1 and what he does in 3:2-3?
ev: Say what is promised in 3:1
Describe the refiner (3:2-3)
Read 3:6
